subject: FintechCo — multi-region performance follow-up & next tests
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha@fintechco.com>, FintechCo Infrastructure <infra@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: FintechCo — multi-region performance follow-up & next tests

Hi Asha / Ravi —

Great to meet earlier today. Short recap from our discovery and the follow-ups we discussed: 

- What we heard: FintechCo needs predictable p95 latency under 200ms for auth/score requests from US/EU/APAC regions, strict data residency for EU customer data, and a simple fall-back routing policy for peak traffic.
- Immediate asks from your side: 1) latency comparison vs your current hyperscaler endpoints (GCP AI Platform + AWS SageMaker), 2) evidence of regional availability & data residency (EU control plane option), 3) a proposed test matrix and timeline.

Next steps (agreed):
1) We’ll run a multi-region perf sweep (warm and cold cache) across US-east1, eu-west1, and ap-southeast1 and share p50/p95/p99 numbers + cost estimates.
2) You’ll share the sample payloads and the endpoint URLs you want us to compare against (we discussed a 128-token score payload and a 512-token prompt).
3) Joint call next week to review results and next-phase: canary Dedicated capacity in eu-west1 for residency testing.

I attached a short latency snapshot (redwood-multi-region-latency-report.pdf) and a first-pass test matrix.

Proposed timing: run tests Mon-Wed next week (2026-09-28 — 2026-09-30). Does that work?

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(jordan.blake@redwood.ai)

--
Attachment: redwood-multi-region-latency-report.pdf (summary of initial dev cluster runs)
Attachment: proposed-test-matrix.xlsx

From: Asha Patel <asha@fintechco.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ravi Menon <ravi@fintechco.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo — multi-region performance follow-up & next tests

Thanks Jordan — really helpful recap. Quick answers and a few clarifications: 

- Payloads: attaching the sample 128-token scoring JSON and a 512-token prompt we use for longer runs (I’ll send via Drive link in a follow-up).
- Comparator endpoints: we want Redwood runs vs our current GCP endpoint (gcp-ai-prod.fintechco.com) and a reserved SageMaker endpoint (aws-sm.fintechco.com). Ravi will copy infra team to provide the exact hostnames and API keys (we’ll provide short-lived keys for the tests).
- Data residency: for EU-specific traffic, we need proof that inferencing and logs can be kept in eu-west1 — not just routing. Can you confirm whether the control plane or data plane touches EU data?

Questions: 
1) For comparators, can you run both cold-start and warm-cache runs?
2) Can you include token-level cost estimates for each run?

Mon-Wed works for us; Ravi will share keys by end of day Monday.

Best,
Asha
Head of Platform Engineering | FintechCo
asha@fintechco.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha@fintechco.com>, FintechCo Infrastructure <infra@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 07:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo — multi-region performance follow-up & next tests

Thanks Asha — quick answers inline and proposed test matrix (summary):

- Data residency: short answer — data plane (inference) can be configured to run entirely in eu-west1 (private deployment / dedicated capacity) so logs and payloads never leave the region. The control plane will still be Redwood-managed, but we offer an EU-hosted control plane for enterprise Private customers; for Dedicated we can provide audit logs showing where KV/cache and model weights were accessed. I’ll have Sean share a short diagram and a compliance note.

- Test types: yes — we’ll run both cold-start (new model server, empty KV cache) and warm-cache (primed KV cache) runs. We’ll also include: small (128-token) and large (512-token) payloads, single-request p95 and 50q concurrent load (q=50) to model peak throughput.

- Cost estimates: we’ll provide token-level egress and per-request cost approximation for each region and compare to the two comparator endpoints.

Proposed test matrix (high level):
- Regions: us-east1, eu-west1, ap-southeast1
- Runs: cold-single, warm-single, cold-load-50q, warm-load-50q
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99, throughput, error rate, cost per 1M tokens

We’ll start the runs today (Mon 2026-09-28) once Ravi shares the short-lived keys. Expected turnaround: 24–48 hours for initial report.

Link to test plan and results folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-perf

If you prefer a short sync after the initial runs, I can schedule 30 minutes Wed morning your time.

Thanks — Jordan

--
Attachment: proposed-test-matrix.xlsx (detailed scenario matrix)

Forwarding the thread — FintechCo wants a side-by-side vs GCP and SageMaker and explicit proof of eu-west1 residency for in-region traffic. Key action items for us:

1) Sean — please prepare a short compliance note + diagram that explicitly states data plane residency options (control plane vs data plane separation) and what we can provide as audit logs. They asked about "whether the control plane or data plane touches EU data" — we need clear language for engineering + infra.
2) Marissa — pricing ask: include token-level cost estimate for run variants and a short note on how Dedicated would change unit economics for eu-west1.
3) Camila — can you prioritize a perf engineer to run the comparator tests (GCP/SageMaker vs Redwood) once Ravi hands keys? They want cold and warm runs, 1s single p95 and 50q load. Aim for initial report within 48 hours of keys.
